steps.message:
Holding off on the edit for a moment — `client.py` isn't staging-only.

`client.py:11` and `client.py:17` are the only two `requests` calls, and both are reached by **both** scripts:

- `scripts/sync_staging.py` → `https://reports.staging.example` (the self-signed one)
- `scripts/export_prod.py` → `https://reports.example.com` (production, nightly finance export)

`verify=False` in `client.py` turns off certificate validation for the production export too, which makes that nightly job accept any certificate — an interception there exposes production report data. The staging cert being self-signed is a real reason to relax verification for staging; it isn't a reason to relax it for prod, and the shared module can't tell them apart on its own.

questions.question: How should TLS verification be handled in client.py?

options.label: Env-gated verify (Recommended)
options.description: Add a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env var (default True) that client.py reads; sync_staging.py sets it to false, export_prod.py keeps full verification. Staging works, prod stays verified.

options.label: Pin the staging CA
options.description: Point verify= at the staging CA bundle path instead of disabling it. Keeps validation on everywhere, but requires the staging cert/CA file to be available on the machines that run the sync.

options.label: verify=False as asked
options.description: Set verify=False on both calls in client.py. Disables certificate validation for the production nightly export as well as staging.

steps.message:
Done, with staging scoped off from production.

- `client.py` reads `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` (default `"true"`) and passes it as `verify=` on both `requests.get` calls.
- `scripts/sync_staging.py` sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=false`, so the self-signed staging cert is accepted.
- `scripts/export_prod.py` is untouched and keeps full certificate validation.

Two notes:

- `ruff check` reports two pre-existing `RUF100` warnings (unused `# noqa: E402` in both scripts, on lines I didn't touch). Left alone as unrelated; say the word if you want them cleaned up.
- The staging run will now emit urllib3 `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call. I didn't add a suppression — tell me if you'd rather silence it.

Nothing committed. No tests exist in the repo, and I didn't execute either script (both point at real hosts).
